How does biodiversity respond and adapt to climate pressures?

Heatwaves, droughts, and heavy rainfall - the negative effects of climate change are already impacting our ecosystems.

But do we understand by how much?

The Amazon rainforest might be closer to a tipping point than scientists thought

go.nature.com/4g7jjnc
posts.external_title: A ‘super’ El Niño could transform the Amazon. Is the world’s biggest rainforest doomed?
posts.external_description: The Amazon rainforest might be closer to a tipping point than scientists thought. Some fear that droughts and fire could nudge it into irreversible decline.

As climate change heats up Europe, experts say countries must shift their focus toward preventing fires, rather than just suppressing them.

Learn more: https://scim.ag/4qaMDhg

The countryside has always been seen as a refuge from the swelter of summer. But now a pioneering study suggests that as global warming continues in much of the world, the countryside's appeal as a climate buffer may dwindle.

Learn more: https://scim.ag/4wna4Fj
